title: Dancing Knights
summary: Improve the king before offering the knight, then preserve the tempo needed to defeat the promotion blockade.

nodes.question: Why block your own pawn with Ka7?
nodes.explanation: White has Ka8, Nc2 and a6 against Kc4 and Nd8. The king must improve before Nb4; otherwise the defender can keep checking and taking the pawn.

nodes.question: How can White dislodge Nb6 from the promotion square?
nodes.explanation: This separately reviewed late source diagram has Kb7, Nb4 and a7 against Kb5 and Nb6. Nd5 attacks the blockading knight while keeping the pawn ready to promote.

branches.title: Improve the king before offering the knight
commentary: Begin from the complete five-piece source board. This selected line stops before the later reset diagrams.
Ka7 blocks the pawn for now, but improves the king’s access to the promotion corner.
Kb5 keeps an eye on a6 and the knight’s next square.
Nb4 offers the knight while preparing to improve the king.
Ka5 is the source’s waiting move, declining the offered knight.
Kb8 leaves the knight offered but approaches c7, where the king can attack Nd8 if needed.
Nc6+ checks and renews the knight blockade.
Kb7 answers the check on the side that preserves White’s exact win.
Nd8+ returns with check.
Kc7 attacks the knight while answering the check.
Ne6+ checks from a different square, but the defender has spent the needed tempo.
Kb8 returns to the promotion corner. The exact position is winning; the later diagram is reconstructed separately rather than linked by invented moves.

branches.title: Move to b8 before preparing Ka7
commentary: Compare the source’s premature king move and pawn push.
Kb8 gives up the exact win by allowing the defender’s checking route.
Kb5 approaches the pawn and prepares the knight blockade.
a7 rushes the pawn while the king and knight are not coordinated.
Nc6+ checks the king and attacks a7.
Kb7 answers the check but cannot save the pawn.
Nxa7 captures the last pawn. The two-knight ending is exactly drawn.

exercises.prompt: Why move the king before offering the knight?
exercises.answer: Ka7 prepares Kb8 and Kc7 with the right timing. In the illustrated premature Kb8 line, ...Nc6+ wins the pawn instead.
It attacks the knight controlling a8. A retreat such as the independently checked ...Nc4 saves that knight but lets White promote.

startContext: The complete five-piece root and a separate late five-piece source diagram are visually reconstructed. The first source line preserves a checked win and the premature Kb8 route draws. The late Nd5 idea is source-based, with ...Nc4 and promotion supplied as an independent representative continuation. Source resets between diagrams are explicitly not treated as a continuous legal sequence.
